  solar system); Cassini-Huygens staged as Saturn (Huygens-on-Titan secondary). Verify the

  target.

  Venus impact; transmitted weak signal ~23 minutes; article lead frames soft landing as
  "successful" but secondary objectives lost). Galileo staged as Success despite high-gain
  antenna failure (orbiter mission completed via low-gain fallback; deliberately deorbited

  per-mission article framing.

  'Cassini–Huygens' uses en-dash (U+2013) per Wikipedia article title. Spot-check naming

Scope checked: `notable_robotic_spacecraft_missions` cycle 1 initial stage. I read the CSV, draft, curation file, and the cited Wikipedia sources. `comments.json` did not exist, so this creates the first audit entry.

Findings

B1. Venera 7 Outcome is not supported by the declared source rule. (factual, BLOCKING)
- CSV row: `Venera 7,1970,Venus,Partial success`.
- Cited master source: Wikipedia `Timeline of artificial satellites and space probes`, 1970 table row, marks Venera 7 target Venus and status `Success` with description `First successful landing of a spacecraft on another planet`.
- Cited per-mission source: `Venera 7` article lead says it became the first spacecraft to execute a successful soft landing on another planet and transmit data back to Earth; the Landing section documents the parachute failure, harder-than-planned impact, weak post-impact signal, and likely sideways orientation, but does not classify the mission outcome as `Partial success`.
- Why blocking: the artifact's own Outcome rule says current/ended mission outcome follows Wikipedia lead or end-of-mission framing. For Venera 7, both the master status and the article lead support `Success`; `Partial success` is a curator assessment of degraded operation, not the declared source-grounded outcome. This changes one CSV value and all outcome-count narrative.
- Minimal fix: change Venera 7 Outcome to `Success`; update outcome distribution from `Success 13 / Ongoing 8 / Partial success 1` to `Success 14 / Ongoing 8`; scrub the Venera 7 open-question/narrative wording. If a used `Partial success` value is desired, add or substitute a mission the master table itself classifies as partial, e.g. Rosetta/Philae or ExoMars/Schiaparelli, with the universe rationale updated.

Checks Passed

- Table integrity: 22 rows × 4 columns, single Mission PK unique, no empty cells, sorted by `(Launch Year ASC, Mission ASC)`.
- Source structure: `source_count=23` and 23 source URLs. The 22 per-mission URLs are present; `claim_type=partially_supplemented`; `proposed_supplements` gives a substantive 22-of-N selection rationale.
- Universe/scope: no Apollo or other crewed mission is staged. The chosen Timeline master is defensible because it covers satellites, space telescopes, and planetary probes; the narrower `List of Solar System probes` is not a better universe source for this mixed satellite/telescope/probe scope.
- Multi-destination spot checks: Voyager 1/2 as `Outer Solar System`, Pioneer 10 as `Jupiter`, and Cassini-Huygens as `Saturn` are defensible under the declared lead-foregrounding rule.
- Row spot checks: Mariner 4 launch year is correctly `1964`; Galileo as `Jupiter` / `Success` is source-defensible; Hubble/JWST/Parker/Curiosity/Perseverance ongoing framing is source-defensible.
- Enums/category: keeping unused `Mercury`, `Comet-Asteroid`, and `Failure` enum values is acceptable because proposed_supplements documents future candidate rows and the active data distribution is clearly stated. `multi_hop` is defensible as a primary category given the documented per-row chaining across article lead, infobox, and end/current-status sections.

Source notes

- Venera evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_artificial_satellites_and_space_probes, 1970 row for Venera 7; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venera_7, lead and Landing section.
- Multi-destination checks: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voyager_1, lead/infobox mission type; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voyager_2, lead/flyby list; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pioneer_10, lead and Jupiter flyby infobox; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassini%E2%80%93Huygens, mission type and Saturn-duration infobox.
- Additional row checks: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariner_4; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galileo_(spacecraft); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hubble_Space_Telescope; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope.
